title: performance(canary): automatic regression detection and rollout guards for perf canary
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: long-running regressions in serving latency introduced by subtle scheduling and batching changes are not always caught by unit/integration tests. This PR adds automated regression detection and rollout guards to the perf-canary pipeline to stop unsafe rollouts and automatically alert engineers when latency/throughput deviates beyond configured thresholds. Changes include a detector that compares canary vs control distributions, configuration for adaptive thresholds, a rollout guard hook integrated with the rollout controller, and observability improvements (timeline + samples) to aid triage.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces a statistical detector that computes rolling-percentile deltas and flags regressions when a configurable significance and effect-size are met. 2) Adds a rollout-guard webhook that prevents canary promotion when the detector is triggered. 3) Plumbs canary context and summaries into the console (per-canary dashboard) for easier triage. 4) Adds end-to-end perf-canary smoke tests and a set of deterministic unit tests for the detector. 5) Adds rollout annotations and audit logs for traceability.

Checklist: - [x] Detector implementation and unit tests - [x] Rollout guard integration with redwood-operator - [x] Console UI: canary summary panel and link to raw samples - [x] Perf e2e tests + CI integration - [x] Release notes drafted - [x] Manual validation on staging cluster

Backwards compatibility: the guard is opt-in by default (canaries created before the feature will not be blocked). Config is exposed via perf-canary configmap and the Redwood Console feature flag.

Notes on thresholds and tuning: default thresholds are conservative (3% median latency regression at p95 with p<0.01 significance) and can be overridden per-customer or per-model. We also add an experimental adaptive threshold mode which scales sensitivity based on baseline variance.

Related: ENG-2345 (perf canary baseline work), ENG-2401 (rollout controller refactor).

review_comments: Ethan Park: Nice work. A few nits on test determinism and an ask to add a low-cardinality metric for 'detector_trigger_count' so SRE can create alerts.
Asha Patel: Addressed the test determinism by seeding the RNG and added the 'detector_trigger_count' metric (instrumented in detector and exposed via metrics endpoint).
Sofia Martinez: Can we have the rollout guard be opt-out per team? I don't want customer rollouts to surprise platform users.
Asha Patel: The guard is opt-in by default; added a config flag in perf-canary/config/defaults.yaml and documented the flag in docs/perf-canary/auto-detection.md.
Priya Nair: Integration looks good. Please add a short blurb to the release notes and include a manual rollback playbook.
Asha Patel: Added release notes and the manual rollback playbook under docs/perf-canary/rollback.md.
E2E CI: integration-perf workflow initially failed due to timing flakiness; reran against staging cluster and all perf checks passed.
changed_behavior_notes: Rollout guard is opt-in by default; can be enabled via perf-canary configmap or Console feature flag.
Default thresholds conservative; admins encouraged to tune per workload.
release_notes: Add automatic performance regression detection for perf canaries. Adds rollout guard to prevent unsafe promotions. Default is opt-in and conservative thresholds are used.
Admins can tune thresholds and enable adaptive mode via perf-canary configmap.
Adds canary dashboard summaries and audit logs for traceability.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives blocking healthy rollouts. Mitigation: conservative defaults + ability to override/disable per-team, and manual override path in Console.
Risk: detector sensitivity may be unstable for low-traffic canaries. Mitigation: adaptive thresholds and minimum-sample gating.
notes_for_release_coordination: Migration: none required. Turning the feature on requires updating perf-canary values in helm and toggling Console flag if desired.
Notify SRE and platform teams so alerts can be onboarded for detector_trigger_count metric.
